Gordon Road Station,
January 4, 1939.

The Yung Sung Club.
- - - - - - - - -

With reference to the attached, I have to report that
the Yung Sung Club, 184 Keng Ka Jau O.O.L. consists of a two
storeyed large Chinese style house which can be approached
by motor car through a broad lane leading west off Yenping
Road near the Stadium. A special garage for the convenience
of guests adjoins the premises. Russian watchmen in uniform
(unarmed) are on duty in the vicinity to prevent the activities
of loafers. A Japanese, presumably the adviser to the Ya Tao
Police inspects the premises every Sunday and the establishment
appears to be comparatively well conducted.

There are two rooms fitted with couches for the con-
venience of opium smokers who are charged $ 50 per pipe.

There are five rooms fitted for gambling and the
following games are indulged in :- Roulette (one wheel only),
Hazard, a game played on the various combinations of three dice,
Fan Tan, Pai Chui and other variations of domino games.

There are two foreigners employed on the premises
one of whom is J. Ezra referred to in D.I. Papps Report. The
other appears to be managing the establishment but I have so
far been unable to ascertain his particulars. The gambling is in
progress 24 hours a day and many Chinese croupiers in a dis-
tinctive uniform are employed.

The place is well frequented by Chinese and
occasionally small foreign parties visit there after curfew
hours. Visits by foreigners are however, the exception rather
than the rule.

荣胜俱乐部。
- - - - - - - - -

关于附件内容，兹报告如下：
荣胜俱乐部位于越界筑路区域（O.O.L.）的孔家角（Keng Ka Jau）184号，由一栋两层楼的大型中式房屋组成，可通过延平路（Yenping Road）体育场附近向西的一条宽阔弄堂驾车进入。 premises 旁附有一个专为客人便利而设的车库。身着制服（未携带武器）的俄罗斯看守在附近执勤，以防止闲散人员滋事。一名日本人（推测为亚陶警察局的顾问）每周日视察该场所，该机构的经营状况似乎相对良好。

设有两间配备躺椅的房间，供鸦片烟客使用，每管收费50元。

设有五间用于赌博的房间，进行的赌博项目包括：轮盘赌（仅一个轮盘）、Hazard（一种基于三个骰子不同组合的游戏）、番摊、牌九以及其他形式的骨牌游戏。

该场所雇佣了两名外国人，其中一人是 D.I. Papps 报告中提到的 J. Ezra。另一人似乎负责管理该机构，但截至目前我未能查明其具体情况。赌博活动全天24小时进行，并雇佣了许多身穿独特制服的中国荷官。

该场所中国顾客众多，偶尔也有小型外国团体在宵禁时间后前往光顾。然而，外国人光顾的情况属于例外而非常态。

本巡捕房首次注意到该场所的存在是在1938年10月15日，当时两名受雇于

Sir,

With reference to the attached, it is a
handbill circulated by the Yung Sheng Club, Lane
175/184, corner of Connaught and Yenping Roads,
which is one of those notorious gambling dens
in the Western district of Shanghai, and received
by this office from an unknown person who, accord-
ing to the writing in black ink thereon, which
is obviously added by him, deplores the deterior-
ating state and condemns the conductor who has
the boldness to disseminate such a handbill to
the general public, contrary to law, requesting
that drastic action be taken by the police in
the interests of peace and good order. Boasting
of an up-to-date accommodation and service to
patrons, the bill states that roulette, and games
of Cantonese "Pai-chiu", "Yao-pao", "Tung-pao"
and "Chao-tan" are played and gambled in the club.

For your information and necessary action
please.

Subject The Yung Sung Club.

Made by __________ and __________ Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

In compliance with the attached memo. from
the D.C. (Special Branch), I beg to submit the following
additional particulars concerning the above named club:-

The Yung Sung Club is located at House 184, Lane
175 Connaught Road near Yongping Road. It is the largest
gambling establishment in the Western area, being equipped with
seven roulette tables. It is owned by a large Chinese
Syndicate and operated under the protection of the Japanese
Authorities as well as the Ta Tao Police Authorities and it
enjoys the special protection of a large gang of loafers.
The running expenses of the club amount to $1,500 daily, of
which amount $250. daily are paid to the Authorities. Owing
to the heavy expenses (squeeze) etc. the club is unable to
make very large profits. It is frequented by many Chinese
gamblers and also by many foreigners, including foreign
women. It was also recently visited by a member of the
Shanghai Municipal Police in uniform (name unobtainable), who
was advised to call in plainclothes next time.

The staff of the club includes a foreigner named
Mr. Joseph Ezra, who is employed in the capacity of foreign
manager and caretaker. Mr. J. Ezra was formerly employed
as assistant by Messrs. Savuk & Co. H.A.I., 128 Museum Road.

A sample of latest type of invitation cards to
the above club is attached.

Subject Assassination of Wong Foo Kwei. (王辅规)
Made by Inspector Shih Sau-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford S.S

At about 8.45 a.m. July 18th, one Wong Foo Kwei alias Wong Shu Ding (王寿萍 ), a very well known loafer and a pro-Japanese element in the Western District, was shot dead in the San Too Lee alleyway (Lane 150, Chinese Number) off Kiaochow Road, O.O.L., by several unknown assailants, whilst he was leaving his home at No.12, San Too Lee alleyway accompanied by two friends.

Whilst the motive of the murder has yet to be ascertained, it will be recalled vide the attached Special Branch report dated March 18th, that Wong, together with one Koo Vung Dao (顧文涛 ) were reported to be the financiers of a gambling den known as the Yoong Sung Company, Kong Ka Jao, O.O.L.

Wong Foo Kwei, it is learned, was formerly an agent to General Yang Hu, formerly Shanghai Woosung Garrison Commander, but following the withdrawal of Chinese forces from the Shanghai Area in November, 1937, he was reported to be working with the Japanese Authorities in the capacity of an informer. He was often seen together with Koo Vung Dao, a former Sub-Inspector of the defunct Shanghai City Government Police Bureau and who is now believed to be an advisor on police affairs to the Shanghai Municipal Administrative Office.

Attached is a name card of Wong Foo Kwei, in which Wong was described as being the Chief of the Investigation Section of the 4th Branch of the First Special District Citizens' Federation, and inspector of eight different factories in the Western District.

At about 3 p.m. on March 16, a tin canister bomb was hurled into a gambling den, 47 Kong Ka Jao off Jessfield Road, O.O.L., by an unknown person. Gambling was in progress and about 50 persons were present at the time of the incident. Superficial injuries were sustained by two female patrons named Zee Wong Sz and Yao Nyi Sz and slight damage was caused to several window panes and furniture. During the commotion that ensued, the culprit made good his escape. Police from the Kong Ka Jao Sub-Station of the Dah Dao City Government Police Bureau, situated at a distance of a few blocks from the den, arrived at the scene and arrested three suspects who were later sent to the Dah Dao West District Branch Police Bureau, 94 Jessfield Road for enquiries. The gambling den resumed functioning shortly afterwards, though according to reports received, the management contemplates removing to house 184 on the same road in the near future.

May 28, 1939.                                          Morning Translation

Shun Pao, Morning Leader and Eastern Times :-

GAMBLING ORGAN PUBLISHES ADVERTISEMENT SOLICITING BUSINESS
UNDER THE PRETEXT OF A DRUG MANUFACTURING COMPANY ; SETTLEMENT
AUTHORITIES WILL TAKE STRICT ACTION FOR SUPPRESSION

    Since the withdrawal of the Chinese forces from
Shanghai, many gambling dens and opium smoking places have
been established in the extra-Settlement roads area in the
Western District. Of late the gambling dens have become
more active. They have invented a new method to mislead
the public by inserting advertisements in newspapers under
the pretext of drug manufacturing companies.
    It appears that recently an advertisement
published by the "Yu Cheng Drug Manufacturing Company"
(有成製素公司) appeared in a local evening newspaper
announcing the sale of a new production of the company known
as Bear's Gall Bladder. It was stated in the advertisement
that the medicine stimulated the brain and improved health,
and in order to push the sale, the company had set aside a
large sum of money for prizes. It was said that coupons
would be given for purchases of not less than 10 cents and
that the drawing of prizes would be held in public and
visits from the public would be welcomed. The advertisement
also invites agents and salesmen for the sale of this
medicine.
    Not knowing the truth of this advertisement,
many have approached the company for the purchase of the
medicine and for the position of salesmen. However, to
their surprise, they found that the so-called drug
manufacturing company is a large gambling establishment
for the conduct of a "Cantonese Style Lottery" on the same
style as the Hwo Hwai Lottery. Three drawings are held
everyday. The so-called "agents" and "salesmen" are in
reality "Ting Doong's" (branches) and "Hong Zai's" (agents)
of the lottery, while the so-called Bear's Gall Bladder
contains in fact the first 80 characters of the book
entitled "One Thousand Words" (千字文). It is due to
the impossibility of publishing advertisements openly that
the gambling den has invented this method to deceive the
newspapers and the public in the name of a drug manufacturing
company.
    As the existence of gambling establishments
and opium smoking dens in the Western District constitutes
a serious menace to peace and order in the community, the
Settlement Police have warned the various gambling dens
to cease operations within a specified time, or else exits
to and from the gambling dens will be closed so as to
prevent the entrance of gamblers. The authorities have
paid special attention to the advertisement of the Yu
Cheng Drug Manufacturing Company and it is said that they
are about to notify the various newspapers to cease
publishing this advertisement. It is also learned that
the newspapers concerned, realizing this treacherous method,
have decided to refuse publication.
    Despite the publication of this advertisement,
the company is still not in a position to do good business
as its treacherous methods are known to the public.

处长

1939年5月28日。                                          晨间译文

《顺报》、《大英晚报》（Morning Leader）和《字林西报》（Eastern Times）：-

赌博机构假借制药公司名义刊登广告招揽生意；租界当局将采取严厉行动予以取缔

    自从中国军队撤离上海以来，西区越界筑路地区开设了许多赌窟和鸦片烟馆。近来，赌窟活动更加猖獗。他们发明了一种新方法，通过在报纸上以制药公司的名义刊登广告来误导公众。
    据悉，最近一家本地晚报刊登了“有成制药公司”（有成製素公司）的广告，宣布销售该公司名为“熊胆”的新产品。广告中称该药能刺激大脑、改善健康，为了推动销售，公司拨出巨款作为奖品。据说购买金额不少于1角者可获得赠券，开奖将公开举行，欢迎公众参观。广告还招募代理和销售人员来销售这种药品。
    许多人不知广告真相，纷纷前往该公司购买药品或应聘销售人员。然而，令他们惊讶的是，他们发现所谓的制药公司其实是一个大型赌博场所，经营着与“回怀彩票”（Hwo Hwai Lottery）风格相同的“粤式彩票”。每天开奖三次。所谓的“代理”和“销售人员”实际上是彩票的“厅东”（分支机构）和“红仔”（代理），而所谓的“熊胆”实际上包含题为《千字文》的书的前80个字。由于无法公开刊登广告，该赌窟便发明了这种方法，以制药公司的名义欺骗报纸和公众。
    鉴于西区赌窟和鸦片烟馆的存在对社区和平与秩序构成严重威胁，租界警方已警告各赌窟在规定期限内停止运营，否则将封闭赌窟的出入口，以防止赌徒进入。当局特别关注有成制药公司的广告，据悉他们即将通知各家报纸停止刊登此广告。另悉，相关报社意识到这种欺诈手段后，已决定拒绝刊登。
    尽管刊登了这则广告，但由于其欺诈手法已为公众所知，该公司的生意依然不佳。

May 26, 1939. Morning Translation

SALES ADVERTISEMENT WITH OFFER OF PRIZES

The "Yu Cheng Drug Manufacturing Company"
(有成製藥公司) on Connaught Road near Zau Ka Tu publishes
the following advertisement in the "Hwa Mei Chen Pao",
the "Sin Wan Pao", the "Shun Pao", the "China Evening
News" (25/5), and the "Ta Ying Yeh Pao" (25/5) :-

Newly Arrived and Specially Made Effective Medicines
Chance to Win $100,000 Prizes Specially Prepared
Bear's Gall Bladder

This Company is selling a reliable and
newly prepared medicine known as Bear's Gall Bladder
which will stimulate the brain and strengthen the stomach.
In order to push its sale, this company has set aside a
large sum of money for prizes.
A coupon will be given for a purchase
of not less than 10 cents. The more you purchase the more
coupons you will get.
The following prizes will be awarded to
winning coupons :-
For a winning 10-cent coupon, a gold ring valued
at $6.20 will be awarded as a prize.
For a winning $1 coupon, a gold watch valued at
$62 will be awarded as a prize.
For a winning $10 coupon, a diamond ring valued
at $620 will be awarded as a prize.
For a winning $100 coupon, a new motor car valued
at $6,200 will be awarded as a prize.
For a winning $1,000 coupon, a large foreign-style
house valued at $100,000 will be awarded as a prize.
The drawing will be held in public.
Visits from the public will be welcomed.

Attention: For particulars regarding
purchases and prizes, write or dial Telephone 21601.
Catalogues are issued.

Agents and Salesmen Wanted

In order to push the sale of Bear's
Gall Bladder, an effective medicine newly prepared by us,
this Company invites agents and salesmen on specially
favourable terms. For particulars, please write or
dial Tel. 21601 and catalogues will be immediately
forwarded.

（批：60. / C.S.Y. / 26/5）

新到特制特效药品
备有十万元奖金
特制熊胆

本公司出售一种可靠且新近配制的名为“熊胆”的药品，该药能刺激大脑、强健脾胃。为促进销售，本公司拨出巨款作为奖金。
购买金额不少于1角者，赠送奖券一张。购买越多，获得的奖券越多。
中奖奖券将获得以下奖品：
中1角奖券者，奖品为价值6.20元的金戒指一枚。
中1元奖券者，奖品为价值62元的金表一只。
中10元奖券者，奖品为价值620元的钻戒一枚。
中100元奖券者，奖品为价值6,200元的新汽车一辆。
中1,000元奖券者，奖品为价值100,000元的大型西式住宅一幢。
开奖将公开进行。
欢迎公众参观。

注意：有关购买及奖品详情，请致函或致电21601。
备有目录索阅。

诚征代理商及推销员

为促进本公司新近配制的特效药“熊胆”的销售，本公司特邀代理商及推销员，条件特别优惠。详情请致函或致电21601，目录将立即寄出。

Made by. D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien, Forwarded by. C. Gonsalves. J. V.

A Cantonese style lottery under the name Yeu
Zung Company (有成) will open a ticket office on
May 10, 1939, at House 1, Tai Ping Li (太平里) (Lane
858) off Jessfield Road, O.O.L. The company which
is reported to be capitalized with a sum of $1,000,000.00
is owned by a Cantonese named Chen (陳). Chu Sung
Ling (朱順林), advisor to the Opium Hong Guild and
concurrently the conductor of the Li Wai Lo Amusement
Club, situated behind the Hollywood Gardens, 1204
Yu Yuen Road, is reported to have been appointed manager
of the new concern.

The company will be operated on similar lines
to other lottery ticket offices earning a commission
from the drawings, except that it will use eighty
Chinese characters in lieu of the numbers. There will
be two drawings a day and tickets will be sold at the
company's main office and its branches which are to
be established in different districts in the near
future.

The proprietor is reported to have obtained a
permit from the Shanghai Amusement Supervision
Department, 9/470 Yu Yuen Road for the conducting
of this business through the assistance of Chu Sung
Ling.

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY
JAN 26 1940
Gaming Den Gang
Seizes Taxi Drivers
Armed Japanese, Chinese Abduct
14 To 15 Jessfield Road House

Attempt Made To Break Boycott Organized
By Chauffeurs Because Of Small Tips
Paid By Autumn Garden Management

Boycott by hire-car chauffeurs of a badlands gambling den was dealt with last night by Japanese and Chinese musclemen, who went out, hired cars and, at pistol point, made the drivers take them to the place, 15 Jessfield Road.

No less than 14 chauffeurs and their cars were detained, and it was not until 10.30 p.m. that representatives of the taxi concerned effected their release. The boycott had been organized because this particular den paid less cumshaw to the drivers than did others.

Autumn Garden
All the gambling dens provide free transport for their patrons. They pay hire-car chits, and also give a tip to the chauffeur. The den at 15 Jessfield Road, known as Chu Yuen, or Autumn Garden, has only been giving the drivers 20 cents.

As the other gaming houses, such as the Hollywood Gardens, give much more in the way of a tip . . . even to $1.50 is reported . . . the chauffeurs of four companies got together and started the boycott. When they picked up a would-be gambler, they would take him to any place except the Autumn Garden. The taxi firms whose chauffeurs organized were Silver Taxi, Taylor, Ford and Johnson.

Strong Arm Methods
The Autumn Garden management last night decided to terrorize these chauffeurs. Japanese and Chinese employees, armed with pistols, were sent out to various places in the International Settlement and French Concession, with instructions to hire taxis and drive back to 15 Jessfield Road. One after another the taxis rolled up at their destination, as the chauffeurs cancelled their announcement that they were not going to the Autumn Garden, when their Japanese or Chinese patron pushed an automatic pistol into the backs of their necks.

Lecture Given
Drivers of taxis were lined up at the Autumn Garden, and given a lecture on the naughtiness of their having started a boycott. They were kept at the place as a punishment.

In the meantime, non-arrival of 14 taxis at various hire-car stations caused increasing anxiety, until a police report showed where they were. Representatives of the firms concerned went to 15 Jessfield Road (which is just outside the Settlement boundary), conferred with the management and managed to get their cars and drivers released.

Most Picturesque
The mansion is one of the most picturesque in Shanghai and is famous in the Chinese community as Sir Elly Kadoorie's Marble Hall and Mrs. Silas A. Hardoon's private garden. Surrounded by a tall wall, the main entrance is decorated with two massive heads of lions made of white granite.

The semicircular driveway leads to the main door, which before the place was converted into a gambling den, opened into a typical Chinese parlor with beautiful blackwood furniture. Paintings by great Chinese masters and scrolls written by famous calligraphists decorated the walls.

Private Gambling
The door on the left led to a sitting room fitted in foreign style while on the right side of the parlor was a room devoted to family mah-jongg and card parties. It is now probably one of the roulette rooms.

Behind the front row of three rooms was a lobby and another spacious sitting room. The most picturesque part of the building, however, is on the second floor. On the left wing was a Turkish room—fitted out all in Turkish style with murals on the wall showing the traditional crescent. There was even a hookah to complete the atmosphere.

Neon Lights
In the center was a spacious foreign style sitting room fitted with neon lights as the room could be converted into a ballroom for a party of at least 150. On the right wing was the dining room in which was a unique dining table. Bored into the one-piece top of the table was a small pond with running water. At formal dinner parties, the pond was filled with water and on the miniature lake, small motor boats and sailing boats floated to and fro as the waiters brought course after course.

The garden was also full of gadgets and contraptions. In a detached small building, part of which was used as the garage and servant quarters, was a winding staircase concealed behind a trapdoor. The owner of the building, Mr. Tan Han-chiu, a wealthy Cantonese merchant, explained that this was all made to satisfy his whims.

Flapping Wings
Surrounded by the drive way was a small fountain with the stone statue of an angel overlooking the spot. The fountain was fitted with reflecting lights with the eyes of the angel could also be lit with electric lights. At the pressing on the button, the wings, made of light metal and painted in the color of the stone, flapped gently.

Mr. Tan's relation with the gambling den, declared to be the most luxurious in the Jessfield Road area, is not known. He may have sold the house, as it is alleged, rented it or have an interest in the new enterprise.

1940 年 1 月 26 日
赌窟帮派
劫持出租车司机
武装日籍、华籍人员绑架
14 至 15 人至杰斯菲尔德路宅邸

试图打破因秋园管理层支付小费过少
而由司机组织的抵制行动

昨晚，日籍和华籍打手处理了租赁车司机对一处法外之地赌窟的抵制行动，他们外出雇用车辆，并在枪口威胁下迫使司机将他们送到位于杰斯菲尔德路 15 号的地点。

不少于 14 名司机及其车辆被扣留，直到晚上 10:30，相关出租车公司的代表才促成他们获释。此次抵制行动的起因是该特定赌窟支付给司机的小费少于其他赌窟。

秋园
所有赌窟均为其顾客提供免费交通服务。它们支付租车凭证费用，并给司机小费。位于杰斯菲尔德路 15 号、被称为“九园”或“秋园”的赌窟，仅支付给司机 20 分。

由于其他赌场，如好莱坞花园（Hollywood Gardens），支付的小费要多得多……据报道甚至高达 1.50 美元……四家公司的司机联合起来开始了抵制行动。当他们接到疑似赌客的乘客时，除了秋园，他们会将其送往任何地方。组织抵制的出租车公司包括银光出租车公司（Silver Taxi）、泰勒公司（Taylor）、福特公司（Ford）和强生公司（Johnson）。

强硬手段
秋园管理层昨晚决定恐吓这些司机。武装着手枪的日籍和华籍雇员被派往公共租界和法租界的各个地方，指令是雇用出租车并驶回杰斯菲尔德路 15 号。一辆接一辆的出租车抵达目的地，因为当日籍或华籍乘客将自动手枪顶在司机后颈时，司机们取消了他们不去秋园的声明。

受到训诫
出租车司机在秋园排成一列，就他们发起抵制行动的不当行为受到训诫。他们被扣留在该处作为惩罚。

与此同时，14 辆出租车未抵达各个租车站点引起了日益加剧的焦虑，直到警方报告揭示了他们的下落。相关公司的代表前往杰斯菲尔德路 15 号（位于租界边界外不远处），与管理层会谈，并成功使他们的车辆和司机获释。

最具特色
这座宅邸是上海最具特色的建筑之一，在中国社区中以埃利·嘉道理爵士（Sir Elly Kadoorie）的大理石厅和哈同夫人（Mrs. Silas A. Hardoon）的私家花园而闻名。四周环绕着高墙，正门装饰着两个由白色花岗岩制成的巨大狮头。

半圆形车道通向正门，在该处改为赌窟之前，正门通向一个典型的中式客厅，配有精美的红木家具。墙上装饰着中国大师的画作和著名书法家的卷轴。

私人赌博
左侧的门通向一间西式布置的起居室，而客厅右侧则是一间专供家庭麻将和牌局的房间。现在这里可能是一间轮盘赌室。

前排三间房间后面是一个门厅和另一间宽敞的起居室。然而，建筑最具特色的部分在二楼。左翼是一间土耳其式房间——完全按土耳其风格装修，墙上的壁画展示着传统的新月图案。甚至还有一支水烟袋以烘托气氛。

霓虹灯
中央是一间宽敞的西式起居室，装有霓虹灯，因为该房间可转换为容纳至少 150 人的派对舞厅。右翼是餐厅，里面有一张独特的餐桌。在一整块桌面中凿刻出一个小池塘，内有流水。在正式晚宴上，池塘注满水，当侍者端上一道道菜肴时，小型摩托艇和帆船在这个微型湖面上来回漂浮。

花园里也充满了各种小装置和机械。在一座独立的小建筑中，部分用作车库和仆人宿舍，隐藏着一个位于活板门后的旋转楼梯。该建筑的所有者、富有的广东商人谭汉秋（Tan Han-chiu，音译）先生解释说，这一切都是为了满足他的奇思妙想。

拍动的翅膀
车道环绕着一个小喷泉，一座天使石像俯瞰着该处。喷泉装有反射灯，天使的眼睛也可以用电灯点亮。按下按钮时，由轻金属制成并涂成石头颜色的翅膀会轻轻拍动。

谭先生与这家号称是杰斯菲尔德路地区最豪华的赌窟的关系尚不清楚。据称，他可能已出售该房屋，或将其出租，或在新的企业中拥有利益。

chauffeur was later treated at the Red Cross General

National Herald and China Evening News :-
"FORD" TAXI DRIVER ASSAULTED BY GAMBLING DEN DESPERADOES.
On January 20, a "Ford" Taxi driver was
assaulted by desperadoes attached to a gambling den.
This has aroused the anger of all taxi drivers in
Shanghai and it is said that they will refuse to drive
passengers to or from the Chiu Yuan (秋園) Gambling Den.
It appears that at about 7 p.m. January 20,
some person ordered a car from the "Ford" Taxi Branch on
Avenue Edward VII, near the Nanking Theatre, which is
operated by Wu Su-ming (吳叔明). When the car, license
No.12345, arrived at the Chiu Yuan Gambling Den, 15
Jessfield Road, the passengers instructed more than 10
desperadoes belonging to the gambling den to assault the
driver who was injured about the head and the right ear.
He was then locked up in a special room.
At about 10 p.m. the "Ford" Taxi Co. sent
members to take the matter up with the gambling den
concerned and the driver was released and taken to the
Chinese Red Cross Hospital on Avenue Haig for treatment.

CONFIDENTIAL S.2, Special Branch. xxxxxx
REPORT. June 6, 39.
Subject: 15 Jessfield Road.

It is rumoured from pro-Japanese sources
that an application has been made to the Japanese
Military for a permit to operate a gambling house at
15 Jessfield Road, the residence of H.C. Tan (譚海秋),
a Cantonese. Repairs are being made to the premises.
One Wong Mow Ting (王茂亭), a leader of the Frenchtown
underworld fraternity, is said to be the principal
investor in the undertaking.

The delay in the issuing of a licence is
being evidently caused by disagreement between the
Secret Service Section of the Japanese Military and
the Gendarmerie. The latter, it is reported, has
control of that Section of the district and is, for
some reason or other, objecting to the issue of a
licence whilst the former is said to have given its
permission.

Endeavours are being made by the promoters to
remove these obstacles.

Further developments will be watched. It may
perhaps be advisable for the Station concerned to keep
an eye on the place in question.

Certified true copy.
H. C. Sandley
